resources.string: Calculate cable length, electrical phase and delay using its velocity factor.
VF is entered manually. The initial value 0.66 is an example, not a specification for your cable. Use the manufacturer’s data or a measurement.
Cable velocity factor and antenna shortening factor are different quantities. Changing one does not change the other.

Model: a uniform cable with constant VF at the selected frequency. Length is measured between reference planes A and B. Connectors and end effects are excluded; verify the finished assembly by measurement. This calculation does not guarantee impedance matching.
A cable between reference planes A and B. Physical length and propagation delay refer to these planes; connectors are not included.
Enter a complete nonnegative decimal number, up to 32 characters. Signs and scientific notation are not supported.
Complete the selected inputs to see the result.
Propagation speed equals cable velocity factor times the speed of light in vacuum.
Electrical angle in degrees equals 360 times frequency times length divided by propagation speed. Delay equals length divided by speed.
Length equals electrical angle in degrees times propagation speed, divided by 360 times frequency.
